title: Earthquake
tldr: During shaking, Drop, Cover and Hold On. Protect your head and neck beneath a sturdy table if nearby; stay indoors rather than running outside. If near the coast, strong or long shaking may mean tsunami danger: move inland and uphill once shaking stops.
steps: Drop onto hands and knees and cover your head and neck. With a mobility device, lock wheels and protect your head.
Stay under sturdy cover until shaking ends. Keep away from windows and objects that can fall.
Move away from buildings and lines. Pull over safely clear of bridges, wires and trees and remain in the vehicle during shaking.
Expect aftershocks; avoid damaged structures and check for fire, gas leaks and tsunami warnings.
next: Check injuries and use texts to communicate. Leave a damaged building by stairs when safe and follow official reentry instructions.
watch: Doorways are not generally the safest shelter. Do not use elevators after damaging shaking.
review_status: source-linked editorial review; not independent expert certification
without_help: After shaking, account for people, put on shoes and check from a safe position for fire, gas smell, damaged wiring and instability. Do not reenter a seriously damaged building while waiting for inspection. Expect aftershocks and keep clear of masonry and power lines.
household: Account for children, older people, pets and anyone who needs assistance before moving. Keep shoes, medicines and a torch in the shelter area. Decide who helps whom and who carries the essential supplies; do not send a lone child to retrieve items.
pack_now: Keep essential medicines, drinking water, a battery light, shoes, phone power and a written contact card within reach. Adapt the load to the hazard and the people with you; do not delay escape to collect equipment.
